label: copy phase: L=3 sequences, or fed-back r/i/l near the end of the copy
explanation: Weak update-gate unit (max excess 0.012) that fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never in the original phase or on the delimiter, and only on repeat occurrences (in_first = 0, as copy inputs always are). It has two loose components. (1) Short sequences: in L=3 sequences it fires on about 20% of copy steps (89% precision at recall_idx 2, i.e. when orig(1) is fed back), and these hold the top activations (e.g. g r j <DEL> g [r]). (2) Fed-back inputs r, i, l (and less so s, y) during the last two copy steps (to_go <= 1) of longer sequences. Activations peak at t = 5 and t = 12. Magnitude is largest for L=3 with in_tok in {r, i, l, s} at recall_idx 2. The disjunction gets dev F1 of about 0.36 (P 0.27, R 0.52, mass recall 0.67). Many copy steps with these tokens stay silent, and about a third of the mass falls outside both clauses (e.g. digits or other letters at mid-copy positions), so this is not a clean description.
